clue.text: Bring back limit in salary for head office in Rome

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the word for salary, which wraps around it

parts.note: pay is a salary; it is split to hold the other piece

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so the word for limit is read right to left

parts.note: a cap is an upper limit, as on spending

explanation.surface: Someone at a head office in Rome is asked to restore a pay cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head office' sounds corporate, but here the office is that of the head of the Catholic Church.
explanation.definitionFit: The papacy is the Pope's office, the headship of the Roman Catholic Church, based in Rome.

clue.text: A poorly organised end of term in which children don't work

indicators.note: badly organised letters have been put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of term

explanation.surface: At the end of term, a messy room where children aren't studying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly organised' reads as one phrase, but 'poorly' is fodder and 'organised' alone signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A playroom is a room set aside for children's games and toys, not lessons.

clue.text: Sympathetic feeling about hospital succinctly expressed

indicators.note: about means around, so the feeling word wraps the hospital letter

parts.note: pity is sympathy for suffering
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A brief, compassionate note about a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside PITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Pithy remarks are concise and forceful, saying much in few words.

clue.text: Fellow-surgeon, perhaps, providing description of light work in theatre

definitions.text: description of light work in theatre
definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; the definition names its use as a description

parts.note: co- is the prefix meaning fellow, as in co-worker
a surgeon is one example of a medic

explanation.surface: A colleague in the operating theatre describes a minor procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests the operating theatre, matching the surgeon, but the definition is about stage comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedic describes comedy, the light, humorous kind of play staged in a theatre.

clue.text: Have meal without a starter?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the meal word goes around the small word

parts.note: to lunch is to have a midday meal
taken as written

explanation.surface: Can you eat a meal and skip the first course?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without a starter' reads as skipping the first course, but 'without' means outside: LUNCH goes round A, and 'starter' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch is the beginning of a venture or the start of a product, so it is a kind of starter.

clue.text: Brisk movement from everyone, therefore, after change of heart

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, and changing it rearranges those central letters

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: Everyone, having changed their mind, sets off at a brisk pace.
explanation.walkthrough: A word's heart is its middle; here only the two central letters of the Latin word trade places. 'Movement' is the musical sense, a section of a symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is a musical tempo marking for fast, lively, and a piece or movement played at that speed.

clue.text: Proposes reform for Minnesota

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, giving the letters a new shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician puts forward reforms for the state of Minnesota.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to put their name forward as a candidate, which is proposing them.

clue.text: Deal with line in letters that he has

indicators.note: the two pieces sit inside the letters named as belonging to he

parts.note: the word he is made of these two letters, split to hold the rest
and means together with
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone copes with a line in a man's correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal with' looks like the definition, but 'with' is needed for its own piece, leaving 'Deal' alone as the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle a matter is to deal with it, manage it, or take care of it.

clue.text: Old man's daily leisure activities

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, the old man; with the possessive it becomes pa's
The Times is a British daily newspaper

explanation.surface: Dad's daily newspaper is what he does for leisure.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is a newspaper, and The Times is the classic British one; 'old man' is slang for father.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastimes are hobbies, the things people do to fill spare time pleasantly.

clue.text: With which consumers are satisfied, with no waiting involved

definitions.text: With which consumers are satisfied, with no waiting involved

parts.words: With which consumers are satisfied, with no waiting involved
parts.note: surface reading: a quick service where customers are happy because there is no queue
setter's reading: diners help themselves, since nobody waits at table for them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Waiting' means serving at table, not standing in a queue: nobody serves the diners, so they help themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: In a cafeteria-style arrangement customers fetch their own food, so nobody waits on them.

clue.text: Some Californian citizens with little time for expression of grief

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is one Californian city
citizens as men, the people of the place
T is the abbreviation for time; with adds it on

explanation.surface: Busy Los Angeles people have no time to mourn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some Californian citizens' is LA MEN, men of Los Angeles; little time is T.
explanation.definitionFit: A lament is a song, poem or cry that voices sorrow or mourning.

clue.text: Show effects of strain in fight

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to wear thin, as nerves or a rope do under stress
second meaning: a battle or brawl

explanation.surface: A fighter shows signs of wear during a bout.
explanation.definitionFit: Fray is a verb for unravelling under stress and a noun for a battle or skirmish.

clue.text: One cover put back with kindness, and with care

indicators.note: something put back goes the other way, so the first two pieces are read right to left

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
a lid covers a pot or box
doing something gently is doing it kindly

explanation.surface: Someone replaces a lid tenderly, taking care.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the numeral and the cover are put back together as one unit, not separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting diligently means working conscientiously and attentively, which is doing things with care.

clue.text: In contract, spot right changes in position for rugby, notably

indicators.note: a single letter, the one standing for right, shifts place within the phrase so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rugby player's contract has a clause about moving positions.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one letter moves: the R (right) leaves 'contract' and lands at the end of 'spot', turning CONTRACT SPOT into CONTACT SPORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby involves deliberate physical collisions between players, making it a prime example of a contact sport.

clue.text: Characteristic energy and sudden movement upset saintly author

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the pieces upside down, so they read in the opposite direction

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy
a dart is a quick sudden movement
St Mark wrote one of the four Gospels

explanation.surface: An author with saintly values is upset by a burst of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns the first two pieces over as a unit; the saintly author is the Gospel writer, so no saint abbreviation is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A trademark is a distinctive feature associated with a person, by extension from a brand's registered symbol.

clue.text: Grave wrecked in utter barbarity

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for utter

parts.note: to utter is to say; it is split to hold the rest

indicators.note: something wrecked is broken apart, so its letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A desecrated grave is an act of complete barbarity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective meaning complete, but it is the verb to say.
explanation.definitionFit: Savagery and barbarity both mean extreme cruelty or uncivilised violence.

clue.text: From other side of the world, area is as natural as it could be

definitions.text: From other side of the world

indicators.note: the letters are arranged as they might possibly be, rather than as given

parts.note: A is the standard abbreviation for area
taken as written

explanation.surface: A distant region looks as unspoilt as can be.
explanation.walkthrough: Area shrinks to A; the rest, 'is as natural', is used whole in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Australasia, Australia and New Zealand with nearby islands, lies roughly opposite Britain on the globe.

clue.text: From southern region, an ancient Greek

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
a part of a country is a region
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek hailing from a southern region.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spartan was a citizen of Sparta, a powerful city-state of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Extended front of ship for missile-launcher

parts.note: something extended is long
the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: An extended ship's bow carries a missile launcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missile-launcher' suggests modern weaponry, but arrows are missiles too.
explanation.definitionFit: A longbow is a tall bow for shooting arrows, which are missiles.

clue.text: Cover for head in meetings about education

indicators.note: about means around, so the meetings word surrounds the abbreviation for education

parts.note: fora is a plural of forum, a meeting for discussion
ED is the abbreviation for education

explanation.surface: A head teacher keeps their hat on in education meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: Fora is the Latin plural of forum, a form crosswords favour over forums.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat with a creased crown, a covering worn on the head.

clue.text: Telling about drug, very enlightening experience

indicators.note: about means around, so the telling word goes round the two short pieces

parts.note: a relation is a telling or narration of events
V is the abbreviation for very
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone recounts a drug trip that felt profoundly illuminating.
explanation.walkthrough: RELATION holds V and E after its first two letters; the pair enters in the order very, drug, the reverse of how they are printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation is a sudden disclosure or insight that opens one's eyes, an enlightening experience.

clue.text: English poet appearing intermittently in Germany

indicators.note: something intermittent comes and goes, so only every other letter shows

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: An English poet occasionally turns up in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray wrote the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gray was an eighteenth-century English poet, author of the famous churchyard Elegy.

clue.text: Country held by Afghan army

indicators.note: the answer is held inside the next words, running across their boundary

parts.note: the letters run from inside the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A nation is in the grip of the Afghan army.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghana is a country in West Africa, formerly the Gold Coast.

clue.text: Where to get drinks in sweltering island capital

indicators.note: the drinks place sits inside the word for sweltering

parts.note: sweltering weather is very hot
a bar serves drinks

explanation.surface: A traveller hunts for a drink in a hot island city.
explanation.walkthrough: The island is Tasmania, the Australian state south of the mainland.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobart is the capital city of Tasmania, the island state of Australia.

clue.text: Couple taken in by European doctor and given a hug

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: being taken in means being held inside, so the pair word goes within the others

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine; it is split to hold the pair
a brace is a pair, as of pheasants

explanation.surface: A couple are welcomed and hugged by a European doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Brace is a word for a pair, used mostly of game birds such as pheasants.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace someone is to take them in your arms, so embraced is given a hug.

clue.text: Questioning how prince can succeed

definitions.note: read as two words, AS KING
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split into two words: a prince succeeds to the throne in the role of monarch

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as AS KING: a prince succeeds his parent as king.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking is the act of putting questions, while the split reading names the role a crown prince inherits.

clue.text: Showing effects of fever, say — wet, in a way

indicators.note: the letters are put in a different manner or arrangement from the one given

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A feverish patient is, so to speak, damp after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like it means 'for example' after fever, but it is fodder alongside 'wet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A high temperature makes the body perspire, so someone with a fever is damp with perspiration.
